bindings.label: Patient developed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules on the upper limbs and body, with subsequent pruritus

A man in his 40s had been diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma the previous year and received 2 courses of radiotherapy to the head and leg and 4 cycles of carboplatin, pemetrexed, and bevacizumab followed by nivolumab (3 mg/kg) every 2 weeks.
After 8 cycles of nivolumab over 5 months, 1- to 2-mm shiny papules appeared on the upper limbs; similar lesions spread to the rest of the body over the subsequent 3 months, followed by pruritus.
Physical examination showed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules scattered on the upper limbs and body, with lesions on the untreated arm coalescing into plaques.
Skin biopsy shows epidermal thinning, basal layer vacuolation, lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and pigment incontinence
Skin biopsy shows no malignant cells or adenocarcinoma metastasis
Immunohistochemical staining was not performed on the skin biopsy specimen
Serum tryptase was elevated at 42 ng/mL and the bone marrow aspirate showed mast cell infiltration
